description: A bursting neuron oscillator on the Hindmarsh-Rose equations: one current control moves it from silence through single spikes to bursts and on into chaos.

params.text: Sets the speed the simulation runs at, over ±4 octaves, with the centre giving C4 at 261.63Hz at the default voicing.
Sets the injected current, 0.4 to 4.0, which moves the cell between quiescent, tonic spiking, bursting and chaos; the chaotic region is around 3.25.
Sets the adaptation rate on a logarithmic scale, 0.001 to 0.05; small values give long bursts and large ones tonic spiking.
Sets the strength of the adaptation, 1.0 to 5.0, which is the depth of the burst.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the injected current.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the adaptation rate.

inputs.text: Adds to the PITCH knob at 1V per octave, setting the speed the simulation runs at.
Modulates the injected current, at a tenth per volt through its attenuverter.
Modulates the adaptation rate in the log domain, multiplying it by a tenth of an octave per volt through its attenuverter.
A rising edge past 1V injects a decaying current pulse, which from a current below threshold starts a single burst.
A rising edge past 1V re-seeds all three state variables at rest, which locks the cell to a clock and gives hard-sync timbres.

outputs.text: The membrane potential, high-passed and soft-clipped to ±5V.
A 10V pulse 1ms long on each spike, so a burst puts out a flurry of triggers.
The slow adaptation variable as a ±5V CV centred on its midpoint: the burst envelope, and not high-passed.

notes: The number of voices follows the V/OCT or TRIG cable, whichever carries more channels; the CV, SYNC and TRIG jacks are all read per channel.
The screen draws the phase portrait: the orbit in the membrane-potential against recovery plane.
menu: Anti-aliasing: Off, ×2 oversampling, ×4 oversampling, ×8 oversampling — sets how many times the simulation is stepped per sample before decimation, and with it the pitch ceiling.
